gaps.sentence: Our guide was highly ___ and had climbed the mountain five times.
gaps.explanation: highly experienced is the standard collocation; 'highly' combines with participial adjectives.

gaps.sentence: Smoking can ___ serious harm to your health.
gaps.explanation: do harm to something is the fixed phrase; 'make harm' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her a compliment on her new hairstyle.
gaps.explanation: pay somebody a compliment is the fixed collocation for praising someone.

gaps.sentence: I was slightly ___ by his rude reply.
gaps.explanation: slightly annoyed is a standard collocation; the other options are too strong to be 'slight'.

gaps.sentence: Make sure you are fully ___ of the terms before you sign.
gaps.explanation: fully aware of something is the fixed collocation meaning knowing completely.

gaps.sentence: Why don't we ___ lunch together on Friday?
gaps.explanation: have lunch is the standard collocation for eating lunch.

gaps.sentence: The children were told not to ___ so much noise.
gaps.explanation: make a noise / make noise is the fixed collocation.
